title: dawn triage notebook - diego
content:
Quick context: woke up to ~5 pages from downstream customers (metrics alert -> increased 5xxs). Paging channel woke me at 04:18. Short log for handoff and my follow-ups.

TL;DR:
- Incident: elevated 5xx rate from inference-router (route: /v1/generate -> backend pool A).
- Impact: ~6% of requests failing for ~18m window, mostly short requests (<64 tokens).
- Mitigation: shifted small-request traffic to pool B (fallback policy), CPU/mem on pool A pods were fine, but kernel OOM events on one pod (node ip 10.24.18.9) caused sporadic restarts.
- Next actions: runbook gaps + ticket RWI-2345 for node hardening & pod eviction tuning.

Timeline (my notes):
- 04:18 pager (PagerDuty): /v1/generate 5xx spike, 5xx% = 6.4, p95 latency up by 120ms.
- 04:20 joined #sre-ops, started triage. Checked Grafana (requests-by-pool, pod-metrics).
- 04:23 noticed pod inference-router-7f9c on node 10.24.18.9 had 2 restarts in last 15m.
- 04:25 kubectl describe pod -> OOMKill on sidecar (log-collector) for that pod; main container kept running but readiness probe flapped.
- 04:27 triggered routing fallback (console -> route policy: small-request -> pool B). 5xx% down to 0.9 by 04:35.
- 04:40 node-exporter showed memory pressure on node 10.24.18.9, dmesg had "Out of memory" lines referencing process containerd-shim.
- 04:55 cordoned node, drained non-critical pods, moved inference-router replacement to healthy nodes.
- 05:10 confirmed recovery and closed active incident.

Immediate findings / hypotheses:
- Sidecar log-collector memory leak (recent image 1.4.2 deployed 2026-09-28) -> OOM on low-memory burst.
- Node-level memory fragmentation or swap pressure due to other workloads (batch jobs) scheduled at night.
- Readiness probe fragility: when sidecar OOMs, main stays alive but probe fails -> short-lived 5xx for requests being routed.

Commands I ran (for handoff):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep inference-router-7f9c
- kubectl describe pod inference-router-7f9c -n inference | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/7f9c-desc.txt
- ssh core@10.24.18.9 sudo dmesg | tail -n 80  # grabbed OOM logs
- kubectl patch virtualservice inference-routing -p '{"spec":{"routes":[{"match":{"fn":"small-req"},"action":{"pool":"pool-b"}}]}}'

Runbook TODOs (gaps observed):
- [ ] Runbook: add explicit check for sidecar OOMs in "inference-router" triage steps (currently only checks main container). -> short instructions + kubectl command snippet.
- [ ] Add a step to check nightly batch-scheduler for heavy jobs before failing over nodes. Link to scheduler: GH action  / cronjobs-dashboard.
- [ ] Add emergency rollback for recent sidecar image 1.4.2 (tagged 2026-09-28). Make quick note how to force older image (1.4.0) for pool A.
- [ ] Update routing fallback playbook to include verification of readiness probe behavior (p95 success, sample request).
- [ ] Add a note to circuit-breaker config: prefer fast-fail on probes rather than immediate 5xx spike (tune threshold).

Follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Diego -> open RWI-2345 for node hardening + eviction tuning (due: 2026-10-07).
- Asha -> investigate sidecar 1.4.2 memory profile + reproduce in staging (linked to PR#412).
- Maya -> add check to runbook and runbook PR (confluence:runbooks/inference-router -> edit).
- Infra -> review nightly batch job placement on node 10.24.* (cc: infra on slack).

Customer comms notes:
- Sent short note to eng-customer-success at 05:22, proposed follow-up with more details after root cause. Keep customers updated if fix (image rollback) is required.

Open questions to chase in morning:
- Which other sidecars were updated on 2026-09-28? (grep image tags across clusters).
- Any node kernel updates recently on that host? (check host maintenance history).
- Is pod memory request/limit appropriate for new sidecar behaviour? Maybe requests too low causing OOM under burst.

Handoff for next oncall (notes for them):
- Incident resolved, pool A now on 3/3 healthy pods; fallback remained active for ~20m.
- If you see similar 5xx pattern: run the sidecar-oom quick check (kubectl logs --previous -c log-collector). If OOM seen -> consider temporary image rollback to 1.4.0: 
  kubectl set image deployment/inference-router log-collector=registry.redwood/log-collector:1.4.0 -n inference && kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-router -n inference
- Ticket RWI-2345 created (link above); infra will take node review; I'll pick up runbook PR in the morning.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Add memory-profiling helm hook for sidecar in staging (run via perf job).
- Consider adding a nightly probe that intentionally hits small-req route to validate readiness probe behavior after deploys.
- Check if autoscaler scales pool A down aggressively at night -> leads to noisy neighbors on same node.

End of log. Quick coffee then sleep. Put these TODOs into my morning list and push runbook PR before noon.

-- Diego
